questions.q: What does this lesson say makes the Meridian Health Network capstone different from just listing course topics?
options: It replaces the need to mention any other course on a resume
It's a specific, built artifact — requirements, workflows, test plans, documentation, and defended architecture decisions — not just a description of topics covered
It is purely theoretical and was never actually built
It is identical in content to the Course 9 CMDB lesson
questions.explain: The capstone is proof through a real, demonstrable artifact, in contrast to a syllabus-style list of topics.

questions.q: Which two CIS specializations did this path build genuine hands-on depth in, per Lesson 2's honest assessment?
options: None — this path built no real depth in any CIS specialization
All four CIS specializations equally
CIS-CSM and CIS-HR
CIS-ITSM and CIS-Discovery
questions.explain: Course 1 and Course 8 built real ITSM depth, and Course 9 built real Discovery/CMDB depth; CSM and HR would start closer to scratch.

questions.q: According to this lesson (reinforcing Lesson 7), what is the actual path toward Technical Architect candidacy?
options: Simply completing more online courses with no real project work
Passing a multiple-choice CTA exam
Real experience across multiple real engagements, not another certification exam
Immediately attempting the CTA assessment right after finishing this path
questions.explain: CTA is a destination credential built on years of real implementation and architecture decision-making, not an exam to cram for.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say staying current with ServiceNow's platform release cycle matters going forward?
options: It's an ongoing professional habit, not a one-time task this path could front-load
It only matters for candidates pursuing CIS-CSM specifically
ServiceNow never changes its platform after a course is finished
This course already covered every future platform release
questions.explain: New releases keep shipping on a regular cycle, so staying current is a continuing responsibility, not something finished once.

questions.q: What is this lesson's framing of finishing this 14-course path?
options: The absolute end of all further learning needed in a ServiceNow career
A guarantee of an immediate Technical Architect role
A real, earned milestone — but a beginning for continued learning and real experience, not a finish line
Equivalent to having already earned a CTA credential
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this as real progress while naming concrete things that still continue afterward: release currency, CIS specialization, and real experience.
